title: Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups
main_claim: For split adjoint exceptional G over a global function field, every local component of a globally generic cuspidal π is tempered, ramified places included. The argument combines three things. (1) The companion unramified Ramanujan result, which makes Ad∘Σ pointwise pure; Deligne Weil II 1.8.4 then gives a pure adjoint WD completion at every place. (2) A local criterion: suppose a generic τ is a Langlands quotient with positive exponent ν. The local-coefficient comparison makes the adjoint L-factor of the twisted tempered completion (r,N_M) regular at 1. The open-orbit argument then conjugates N_M to the pure N_*. Purity on the nilradical forces |det|=1, but the ν-twist forces |det|<1. (3) A Langlands–Shahidi coefficient comparison that does not depend on monodromy, proved using multiplicativity, Tate factors, Gan–Lomelí globalization and Lomelí's crude functional equation.

issues.description: The argument depends on the cited form of GHS: an essentially tempered completion of the Genestier–Lafforgue parameter for every tempered representation of a Levi, in every characteristic. The upgrade from essentially tempered to tempered is argued correctly. I could not check offline that the cited GHS statements cover arbitrary tempered representations without extra hypotheses.
issues.evidence: The paper gives an explanation of the cited form, not a proof; the GHS statement was not checked against the source.

issues.location: Sec 4.4, eq. (crude-functional-equation), citing Lomelí arXiv:1507.03625 Thm 4.3
issues.description: The cited preprint is titled for unitary groups. The proof needs the crude functional equation for arbitrary maximal Levi pairs (H,M) inside split exceptional groups. Lomelí's general framework very likely supplies this, but the paper does not say where the general statement lives.
issues.evidence: Bibliography: 'The Langlands–Shahidi method over function fields: Ramanujan Conjecture and Riemann Hypothesis for the unitary groups'.

coverage: Read the whole paper (6 sections). Checked by hand: Lemma 3.1 monodromy-ratio identity (R_0/R_N=∏(-xc), with dual eigenvalues Qc^{-1} and direction verified); the purity lemma and the sign conventions of the example; Prop 3.3 (the Killing-form transpose e_Q→e_1 is injective iff the adjoint L-factor is regular at 1); Lemma 2.1 (char-2/3 polynomial argument; computed that the B2 char-2 commutator span is everything); Whittaker-family specialization; the elementary factorization and positivity of the slopes c_j; consistency of the ε/ratio direction between the crude and Galois functional equations; the generic-regularity proof (n gives arguments 1+b(ν), n^- ≅ n^∨ gives 1−b(ν), and having no zeros forces each numerator factor to be regular); the determinant contradiction; Deligne 1.8.4 weight conventions with geometric Frobenius. Confirmed that companion Cor 1.2 matches the stated Thm 6.1 (the sibling audited it at rank 83: no gap, but it relies on Ciubotaru–Harris). Cited theorems (GHS, Gan–Lomelí, Lomelí, Genestier–Lafforgue) were taken on trust.
sibling_notes: Conditional on the companion Ramanujan–Arthur Decompositions paper (rank 83, no_gap_found; the sibling flagged that it relies on Ciubotaru–Harris Cor 6.32(1)). The statement of Cor 1.2 there matches its use here exactly.
